documents.title: github.com/stretchr/testify
documents.description: Module testify is a set of packages that provide many tools for testifying that your code will behave as you intend.
documents.searchText: module testify is a set of packages that provide many tools for testifying your code will behave as you intend. contains the following packages: [github.com/stretchr/testify/assert](https://pkg.go.dev/github.com/stretchr/testify/assert) package provides comprehensive assertion functions tie in to [the go testing system](https://go.dev/doc/code#testing). [github.com/stretchr/testify/require](https://pkg.go.dev/github.com/stretchr/testify/require) same assertions but fatal checks. [github.com/stretchr/testify/mock](https://pkg.go.dev/github.com/stretchr/testify/mock) system by which it possible mock objects and verify calls are happening expected. [github.com/stretchr/testify/suite](https://pkg.go.dev/github.com/stretchr/testify/suite) basic structure using structs suites, methods on those tests. includes setup/teardown functionality way interfaces. [golangci-lint](https://golangci-lint.run/) compatible linter available called [testifylint](https://github.com/antonboom/testifylint).

documents.searchText: package require implements the same assertions as assert but stops test execution when a fails. ### example usage following is complete using in standard function: import ( "testing" "github.com/stretchr/testify/require" ) func testsomething(t *testing.t) { var string = "hello" b require.equal(t, a, b, "the two words should be same.") } have global functions package, instead of returning boolean result they call [testing.t.failnow](https://pkg.go.dev/testing#t.failnow). consequence this that it must called from goroutine running function, not other goroutines created during test. every assertion function also takes an optional message final argument, allowing custom error messages to appended method outputs. ## condition ```go condition(t testingt, comp assert.comparison, msgandargs ...interface{}) ``` uses comparison complex condition. conditionf conditionf(t msg string, args contains contains(t s interface{}, asserts specified list(array, slice...) or map substring element. require.contains(t, "hello world", "world") ["hello", "world"], {"hello": "world"}, "hello") containsf containsf(t require.containsf(t, "world", "error %s", "formatted") "hello", direxists direxists(t path checks whether directory exists given path. fails if file rather there checking exists. direxistsf direxistsf(t elementsmatch elementsmatch(t lista listb lista(array, equal listb(array, ignoring order elements. are duplicate elements, number appearances each them both lists match. require.elementsmatch(t, \[1, 3, 2, 3], 2]) elementsmatchf elementsmatchf(t require.elementsmatchf(t, 2], empty empty(t object value "empty".
